title: Design Challenge
intro: Teams combine solo sketches into one paper cupcake that shows the qualities of a strong team.

blocks.title: Mission
blocks.text: Create ONE paper cupcake design that represents teamwork, communication and creativity.

items: Print the Print Pack: one Design Challenge Card and one Design Your Cupcake Worksheet per team
Blank paper for each student’s solo sketch
Pencils, markers and coloured pencils; a timer the class can see
Tables for teams of 3–4, with room for every solo sketch and one team worksheet in the middle

items.title: Launch
items.text: Give each team a Challenge Card. Read the mission aloud: one team cupcake, three teamwork qualities, one shared decision.

items.title: Sketch alone
items.text: Students sketch on blank paper without talking. Symbols, colours, words and illustrations all count.

items.title: Share ideas
items.text: Each student shows one idea. Teammates ask one question and name one idea they want to keep.

items.title: Agree and design
items.text: The team draws ONE cupcake on its worksheet, shows at least three teamwork qualities, and agrees on one shared decision to explain.
prompts: What can we keep from both ideas?
Who hasn’t added an idea yet?

items.title: Clean up
items.text: Collect each team’s sketches and worksheet together; put supplies away.

items.title: Explain one decision
items.text: Each team explains the meaning behind its cupcake and one choice it made together, by speaking or pointing to the drawing.

items: Every student sketches an idea before team talk.
The team completes ONE worksheet that keeps at least one idea from each sketch.
The design includes at least three teamwork qualities, named or drawn.
The team can explain the meaning behind its design and one choice it made together.

blocks.text: Teamwork qualities students might show: communication, inclusion, creativity, trust, collaboration. The activity is an example; adapt materials or format to fit your class.

items.text: Every student adds an idea from their sketch, not only the loudest voice.
Teammates ask about each other’s sketches and build on ideas instead of replacing them.
The team gives up one idea to keep another, and says why.
The team changes its plan when an idea does not fit, without starting over.
Each person names one thing from their sketch that must stay.
Keep the base from one sketch and the decorations from another.
A student can describe ideas aloud or point while a teammate draws.
